# Package structure

Here we want to summarise discussions about the structure of the
package, design decisions around functions, and their relationship with
the cross-referencing process.

## User journey

For the package design we distinguish two main stages of the
cross-referencing process. The first is dedicated to data preparation,
validation and exploration. The second is dedicated to analysis and
synthesis. See [Figure 1](#fig-userjourney) for an overview.

``` mermaid
flowchart TB
    PREP["Data Preparation:<br/>importing, joining, filtering, modifying datasets "]:::Mixed
    VALID{"Data<br/>Validation"}:::InPkg
    EXP[Exploration:<br/> Interpreters, rounds, membership values]:::InPkg
    NINT{"No. interpreters<br/> and rounds"}:::InPkg
    ELI1[Within rounds<br/>agreemnet]:::InPkg
    ELI2[Between rounds<br/>entropy metrics]:::InPkg

    FILTER["Between rounds<br/>entropy metrics"]:::InPkg
```

Figure 1: Steps of the user journey. Solid green symbols can be
completed with the package functions, classes and methods. Dashed
symbols require a mix of package functions, other packages, and external
tools.

The ecoSynthesis package aims to facilitate the tasks related to these
stages of the cross-referencing process. While some task could be
completed with the functions, classes and methods defined in this
package, there are some task that will require interaction with
additional R packages, other tools, and the real world.

## Functions, classes and methods

This package includes functions, classes and methods. Some functionality
has been **proposed** and tested outside the package development
process. Some of these proposals are integrated in **development
branches** before they are implemented in the **main branch**.

We use a consistent key to refer to these in all figures
[Figure 2](#fig-legend).

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Figure 2: Visual key to functions, classes and methods in different
stages of development.

### Core functions

Two core functions
([`lookup_tbl()`](https://ecosystem-indicators-workflows.github.io/ecoSynthesis/reference/lookup_tbl.md)
and
[`membership_tbl()`](https://ecosystem-indicators-workflows.github.io/ecoSynthesis/reference/membership_tbl.md))
create the main classes used in the package. All other functions will
work with these two main classes.

> **Warning**
>
> Documentation of the classes is missing in the R files!

Figure 3: Core functions (blue), classes (gold), methods (green) and

### Data preparation

We propose a couple of simple functions to facilitate the most common
data import nad data cleaning steps.

> **TO DO**
>
> Two proposed functions *membership_clean()* and *read_membership()*.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Figure 4: Data preparation: functions (blue), classes (gold), methods
(green) and their relationship during a cycle of data preparation.

However, in many cases data preparation will require wrangling with data
formats (e.g. combining or joining data, filtering, modifying records).
This can be done effectively inside R (for example with packages from
the `tidyverse` collection), or outside R with other tools of
preference.

### Validation pipeline

Data validation allows the user to check if the data is valid for
further processing. The validation functions are intended to catch
common problems and pitfalls that could invalidate the final results.
Validation should be completed before moving to data exploration and
analysis.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Figure 5: Validation pipeline: functions (blue), classes (gold), methods
(green) and their relationship during a cycle of validation.

Positive results of validation means that the process can move to the
step of data exploration, negative results indicate that further steps
of data preparation are required.

### Exploration

Data exploration includes calculating basic statistics to understand the
shape of the data, for example the No. of interpreters and rounds, or
the distribution of membership values.

> **TO DO**
>
> Plot classes, summaries and other tools for exploration.
>
> Add figure with existing and proposed functions

Data exploration could lead to identifying gaps or other shortfalls in
the data. In such cases, an additional step of data preparation (and
validation) might be useful before proceeding with next steps.

Data exploration will provide the basic data to inform decisions about
the analysis and synthesis steps.

### Analysis

Analysis steps will depend on the number of interpreters and rounds.

With one interpreter and one round, proceed directly to synthesis and
outputs.

With one interpreter and multiple rounds, it is possible to analyse how
uncertainty (measured as entropy) changes between rounds.

With multiple interpreters it is possible to analyse agreement and
disagreement between experts in a single round, and analyse changes in
uncertainty and disagreement between rounds. We refer to this process in
general as *expert elicitation*, although the specific methods used for
the consultation of interpreters can be different in different contexts.
